title: Stale Snapshot Illusion via Blind Writes
damaged_code:
```sql
-- Transaction 1
SELECT price FROM inventory WHERE id = 1; -- Reads $10
-- Transaction 2 concurrently updates price to $20
-- Transaction 1 blindly writes back based on stale value
UPDATE inventory SET price = 10 * 1.1 WHERE id = 1; -- Price set to $11, losing $20
```
pattern: Performing an update to a database row or shared memory value based on a previously read snapshot without checking if the value was modified concurrently.
why_bad: It allows stale reads to overwrite up-to-date concurrent writes, causing lost updates and data inconsistency.
detection: A read operation followed by a write to the same identifier where the write does not include a comparison to the read value or use a CAS pattern.
counterexample: Optimistic concurrency control (OCC) using version stamps or conditional checks.
fix:
Use a conditional write check on the expected version or value.
```sql
UPDATE inventory SET price = 11, version = 2 WHERE id = 1 AND version = 1;
```
